### What is a **Large Language Model (LLM)?** | Concept | Short answer | Key points | |---------|--------------|------------| | **Definition** | A neural‑net architecture, usually a transformer, that has been trained on billions of tokens of text. | • Learns statistical patterns, syntax, and factual knowledge.
• Capable of generating fluent text, answering questions, translating, summarising, etc. | | **Tracing its roots** | The transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017) made everything possible. | • GPT‑*n* (OpenAI) – autoregressive, generation‑first.
• BERT (Google) – masked‑language‑model, understanding‑first. | | **Why “large” matters** | Size (parameters + training data) correlates with ability to store more knowledge & nuance. | • GPT‑4 ~ 100 billion params (approx).
• LLaMA‑2‑13B ~ 13 B param; 70 B is another tier. | --- ## 1. Core Technical Families of LLMs | Family | What it does | Example models | Primary use | |--------|--------------|----------------|-------------| | **Autoregressive** | Generates next token conditioned on all previous tokens. | GPT‑3, GPT‑3.5, GPT‑4, LLaMA‑2‑13B, Pythia | Text generation, conversation, code,
